g3-doc-idiom.title: Task 3a: document the no-park idiom in crew-dispatch.md
g3-doc-idiom.imperative: Reasoning gate, crew-waived (documentation-only, no independently-verifiable behavior beyond a grep-checkable presence, and LAUNCH_ORDER forbids crew dispatch this run). Add a section to skills/commander/references/crew-dispatch.md stating plainly: the Commander's own process ends with its turn; the agent harness can auto-background a long-running foreground Bash call (e.g. the full suite, ~2 minutes); a harness-backgrounded command is therefore not awaitable, and 'wait for the notification' is never a valid way to end a turn. Give the working idiom by name, concretely for the full-suite check (nohup + until-grep poll + tail), and name the fallback: spine_halt block with the crew id recorded, so a parent resumes deliberately (E1 fail-up).

g4-stop-hook-decision.title: Task 3b (optional): attempt or decline the Stop-hook mechanical check
g4-stop-hook-decision.imperative: Reasoning gate. Evaluate feasibility of a Stop-hook condition refusing turn-end while the bound spine has an in-progress gate and a running crew whose pid is not live, per LAUNCH_ORDER's explicit proof requirement: attempt ONLY if both a red (fires on the parked shape) and a control (does not fire on a legitimate turn end) are producible; otherwise decline with reasons -- a fully acceptable outcome. Read scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py's Stop handler and its fail-open posture first. If declining, record the specific reason (the feasibility finding from context/understand: handle_post_tool_use only establishes a session->spine binding for a Bash checklist_engine.py claim, never for the MCP door spine_lease tool that is this repo's own documented default -- so decide_stop's existing mid-flight block, which any new pid-liveness clause would extend, is already inert for MCP-door sessions; extending it would ship a check that cannot fire for the dominant current dispatch path, and closing that root gap is a second subsystem outside this run's budget) and flag it as a triage candidate for the triage step.

postconditions.statement: 3b shipped with a proven red+control pair, OR declined with the specific reason recorded and flagged to triage

constraints: only under decision to attempt: scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py's Stop handler + its tests
fail-open posture (Pre-Ruling 4) must be preserved if attempted

payload.reason: handle_post_tool_use (scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py) only establishes a session->spine binding when a session claims via a Bash 'checklist_engine.py claim' command (matcher: Bash on the PostToolUse hook). This very session claimed its own lease via the MCP door (spine_lease tool, this repo's own documented default per spine.json's init imperative), and no binding was ever recorded for it -- verified directly: ran 'python3 scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py Stop' by hand against this session_id and got an empty {} (allow), and no session/spine binding file exists in this worktree at all. decide_stop's EXISTING mid-flight block already refuses ANY turn-end while a bound spine has a non-terminal, non-blocked gate under an active lease -- it does not need a new pid-liveness clause to catch the auto-backgrounded-crew-park shape, since that shape IS mid-flight. The gap is not decide_stop's logic; it is that the binding precondition it depends on is never established for MCP-door sessions. Building the pid-liveness clause LAUNCH_ORDER proposes on top of that would ship a check indistinguishable, in the dominant current dispatch path, from not shipping it at all -- a check whose output is identical in the healthy and defective world for most real dispatches is worse than an honest decline (global-orchestrator.md, 'a check that cannot fail'). Wiring the MCP door's claim/release into spine_rail's binding store (or widening PostToolUse's matcher to MCP tool calls) is a second, distinct subsystem outside this run's budget and outside the Yours file-ownership fence (touches scripts/mcp_spine_server.py and/or .claude/settings.json's hook matcher, neither listed). Declining 3b; flagging the binding gap as a triage candidate.
